Content: AES-256-CBC with a random IV per file, plus a trailing HMAC-SHA256 tag (the entry id is authenticated too, so renamed ciphertext fails verification).
Keys: the password is run through PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (210k iterations) to derive a KEK that wraps a random master key — so changing the password only rewrites a 157-byte header, not the files.
Folder: HexFile/.vault (dot-prefixed; most file managers and galleries skip it).
Limits: no screenshot blocking, no full-disk encryption; delete only removes ciphertext without overwriting, so forensic recovery of flash remnants may still be possible.

"Android does not let an ordinary app read another app's current screen; only an accessibility service can learn which app opened which Activity.

Open Settings → Accessibility → HexFile Activity log and turn the switch on; recording starts automatically when you come back.
